topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic sets up the structure and learning goals for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and systemic limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and non-targeted cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside the systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms that constrain them.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular defects and vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss targeted strategies that leverage specific intrinsic weaknesses of cancer cells, such as hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibition and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases with small-molecule inhibitors, detailing mechanisms of action, off-target effects, and pathways of acquired resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and targeted drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe antibody-based strategies that selectively bind surface antigens to directly impede tumor signaling or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interaction between tumors and the host immune system, encompassing natural immune surveillance, immune checkpoint inhibition, and engineered T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Historical progress, future paradigms, and clinical challenges
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad perspectives on cancer mortality trends, treatment resistance, future diagnostic and therapeutic paradigms, and ethical dilemmas in clinical trial design.
